title: Save the details to the file
one: Put one line in the file, clear Global.cs, start again.

screens.title: Check the parts this chapter needs
screens.goal: Before I start, I check the group, the Save button and Global.cs.

blocks.p: This chapter uses work from earlier chapters. This screen checks that it is there.

check.what: Is chapter 10 done, so a group appears when you click Calculate?
check.how: Run the program. Do every part, then click Calculate.

check.what: Is there a Save button under the panels, named btnSaveDetails?
check.how: Open frmDataEntry in the Design tab. Click the Save button and look at its Name.

check.what: Does Global.cs have all fourteen names?
check.how: Double-click Global.cs in Solution Explorer. Count the lines that start with public static.

screens.title: Let the form use files
screens.goal: One line at the top of frmDataEntry's code lets this form use the file tools.

blocks.p: Open frmDataEntry's code. Scroll to the very top. The top lines start with the word using. Click at the end of the last one and press Enter.

code.title: One line at the top
code.where: under the other using lines, at the very top of frmDataEntry's code
partLines: The file tools
It lets this form use File, which writes to a file.

blocks.p: Without [[using System.IO|0]] the word File goes red.

words: A line at the top that lets the form use the file tools.
A wavy line. It sits between the pieces of a line, like a fence.
The end of a line. The next words start on a new line.
Adds words to the end of a file. It makes the file if it is not there.
blocks.intro: Four new words in this chapter. Click a marked word to see what it means.

frames.title: The using line at the top

frames.alt: The top of frmDataEntry.cs with using System.IO typed under the other using lines
frames.say: The new line sits under the other using lines.

screens.title: Save only when all five panels are switched off
screens.goal: The Save code only goes ahead when all five panels are grey.

blocks.p: In the Design tab, double-click the Save button. A panel is switched off when its part is done.

code.title: The Save button, part 1 of 6
code.where: between the curly brackets of btnSaveDetails_Click
partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given
Are all five panels grey?
One long line. && means and. All five must be switched off.
Room inside
A curly bracket, then two empty lines. The saving goes here later.

blocks.watch: Line 3 is one long line. Keep it on one line in Visual Studio.

screens.title: If a panel is still on, stop
screens.goal: If any panel is still on, a message shows and nothing is saved.

blocks.p: Click on the second empty line inside the if. The line numbers jump to 46, because the saving fills the gap later.

code.title: The Save button, part 2 of 6
code.where: under the two empty lines inside the if
partLines: End the if
Two empty lines, then the curly bracket that ends the if.
Not done? Say so and stop
else runs when a panel is still on. A message shows and return stops the code.
An empty line
Leave one empty line here.
Visual Studio wrote this line
This curly bracket is the end. Your code goes above it.
given

blocks.watch: The saving goes on the empty lines inside the if. The next screens fill them.

stages.title: Write the line to the file

screens.title: Join all the details into one line
screens.goal: All eleven details join into one line, with a ~ between each piece.

blocks.p: Click on the first empty line inside the if. Each [[~|1]] is a fence between two pieces.

code.title: The Save button, part 3 of 6
code.where: on the first empty line inside the if of btnSaveDetails_Click
code.text:
//create the string with each value separated by '~'
        string record = Global.surname + "~" +
        Global.firstname + "~" +
        Global.quizScore.ToString() + "~" +
        Global.yearGroup + "~" +
        Global.gender + "~" +
        Global.average.ToString() + "~" +
        Global.attempt1.ToString() + "~" +
        Global.attempt2.ToString() + "~" +
        Global.attempt3.ToString() + "~" +
        Global.reactionTestScore.ToString() +"~" +
        Global.assignedGroup;
partLines: A note
A note about the fences. It does not run.
The first five pieces
Surname, first name, quiz score, year group and gender, each followed by a ~.
The last six pieces
The average, the three attempts, the test score and the group.

drawn.alt: The line Smith~Anna~4~12~F~6.33~5~6~8~5~Advanced. Each piece has its own colour and a number from 0 to 10.
drawn.say: The order matters. The report reads the pieces back in this order.

screens.title: End the line and write the file
screens.goal: The line ends, goes on the end of the file and a message says it is saved.

blocks.p: [[Environment.NewLine|2]] ends the line. [[File.AppendAllText|3]] adds it to the end of the file.

code.title: The Save button, part 4 of 6
code.where: under part 3, inside the if of btnSaveDetails_Click
partLines: End the line
An empty line and a note. Then the end of a line is added to record.
Write it to the file
An empty line and a note. Then record goes on the end of the file.
Say it is saved
A message tells the pupil it worked. Empty lines sit either side.
code.yours: MY file is pupilStats.txt. If YOU choose another name, type it in place of pupilStats.txt. The report needs the same name.

screens.title: Clear Global.cs, first half
screens.goal: The first seven names in Global.cs go back to empty, ready for the next pupil.

blocks.p: Global.cs still holds this pupil's details. Clear them, so the next pupil starts empty.

code.title: The Save button, part 5 of 6
code.where: under part 4, inside the if of btnSaveDetails_Click
partLines: A note
A note about clearing. It does not run.
Empty words
Words go back to two speech marks with nothing between them.
Back to the start
averageCalculated goes back to false. The average goes back to 0.

screens.title: Clear the rest and start again
screens.goal: The other seven names are cleared, the form closes and a fresh data entry form opens.

blocks.p: Each number goes back to 0. Each true or false goes back to false.

code.title: The Save button, part 6 of 6
code.where: under part 5, inside the if of btnSaveDetails_Click
partLines: The other seven
The attempts, the test, the two true or false names and the group.
Start again
An empty line. Then this form closes and a fresh one opens.

drawn.alt: The data entry form, fresh and empty, beside Global.cs.
drawn.say: The file keeps the line. The form starts fresh for the next pupil.

screens.title: Try your Save button
screens.goal: I save two pupils, find the file and check it has two lines with fences.

blocks.p: Run your program. Log in and do every part. Click Calculate. Then try each row. The Find the file box shows the Debug folder.

check.how: The saved message shows. Then a fresh data entry form opens.

check.what: Stop the program. Find the Debug folder. Look for YOUR file.
check.how: YOUR file is there, next to the program.

check.what: Double-click YOUR file. It opens in Notepad.
check.how: One line, with a ~ between each piece.

check.what: Run again and save a second pupil. Open the file again.
check.how: Two lines. The second pupil is on the second line.

check.what: Log in and click Save straight away.
check.how: The not all results message shows. NO line is added to the file.
